levels.title_en: Heat, pain, fever — and a second verb

items.pronunciation_notes: The र closes the first syllable rather than opening the second: gar-mii.
items.gloss_en: to feel hot — literally, for heat to be felt

learn.title_en: गर्मी splits the same way ठंड did
learn.explanation_en: गर्मी is feminine, so लग रही है, exactly like ठंड. And it splits the same two ways: मुझे गर्मी लग रही है is about you, गर्मी है is about the weather. One extra thing is worth knowing — गर्मी also means summer, so गर्मियों में is "in summer". The same word covers the season, the temperature and the sensation, and the grammar around it tells you which one is meant. Avoid मैं गर्म हूँ: it describes your body temperature to somebody touching you, and it is not how anyone says they feel hot.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me heat is being felt.

examples.note: About you.
About the weather. No dative anywhere.

examples.hindi: गर्मियों में बहुत गर्मी लगती है।
examples.read_as: garmiyoṁ meṁ bahut garmii lagtii hai.
examples.english: It feels very hot in summer.
examples.note: Oblique plural गर्मियों for the season, and the sensation word again at the end.

common_error.why_en: मैं गर्म हूँ says your body is hot to the touch. It does not say you feel hot.

practice.question: ___ गर्मी लग रही है।
practice.explanation_en: Heat is felt at a person, so the person takes को.

game.explanation_en: The first is about your body temperature. गर्मी is feminine, so लग रही है.

tts_strings: गर्मियों में बहुत गर्मी लगती है।

items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable: dard. The द is dental, made with the tongue against the teeth.
items.gloss_en: to be in pain — literally, for pain to happen

learn.explanation_en: The verb changes here, and this is the first real fork in the module. Sensations that wash over you take लगना — भूख, प्यास, ठंड, गर्मी. Conditions you are in take होना — दर्द, बुखार. So it is मुझे दर्द हो रहा है, never लग रहा है. दर्द is masculine, so everything downstream is masculine: हो रहा है, हुआ, होता है. You will also hear मेरे सिर में दर्द है, "in my head there is pain", which uses में and a possessive instead of the dative. Both are current Hindi; the दर्द होना version is the more general one and the one to learn first.

examples.note: दर्द is masculine, so हो रहा.
The other construction — में on the body part, no dative.
Noun experiencer, perfective.

common_error.why_en: दर्द is a condition, not a sensation felt on the surface, so it goes with होना.

practice.question: ___ दर्द हो रहा है।
practice.explanation_en: वह goes oblique and fuses with को to give उसे.

game.explanation_en: दर्द takes होना and is masculine, so हो रहा है.

items.pronunciation_notes: ख is aspirated: bu-khaar, with the length on the second syllable.
items.gloss_en: to have a fever — literally, for fever to be

learn.explanation_en: बुखार takes होना like दर्द, but usually in its plainest form: मुझे बुखार है. No लगना, no रहा, just है. बुखार is masculine, so the past is मुझे बुखार था. Together with मुझे दर्द हो रहा है this is what you say at a doctor's, which makes it worth over-learning. Notice once more what Hindi does not have: there is no adjective for "feverish" any more than there was one for "thirsty". The noun does the work, and the dative puts you where it lands.

examples.note: The whole sentence is three words.
बुखार is masculine, so था.
Noun experiencer, oblique plus को.

common_error.why_en: मैं बुखार हूँ says you are a fever. The fever is the subject and you are where it is.

practice.question: ___ बुखार है।
practice.explanation_en: The fever is the subject; you are the place it is.

game.explanation_en: मुझे बुखार है. The third option keeps हूँ, which would be agreeing with the speaker; the fourth uses लगना, which बुखार does not take.

summary.recap_en: गर्मी completes the लगना set and splits like ठंड — मुझे गर्मी लग रही है is you, गर्मी है is the weather. दर्द and बुखार introduce the second verb: conditions take होना, and both are masculine, so हो रहा है and है.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the third verb — things that arrive rather than being felt.

items.pronunciation_notes: The vowel is long and nasalised at once: niiṁd, one syllable.
items.gloss_en: to be sleepy — literally, for sleep to come

learn.explanation_en: Third verb, third relationship. Things that come over you from outside take आना: नींद, ग़ुस्सा, हँसी, याद. मुझे नींद आ रही है — literally, to me sleep is coming. नींद is feminine, so आ रही है. It is worth holding the three-way split as a picture rather than a list: लगना is felt on you, होना is true of you, आना arrives at you. Textbooks present these as unpredictable idioms to be memorised one at a time. They are mostly not, and a learner who has the picture can guess correctly far more often than one who has the list.

examples.note: नींद is feminine, so आ रही.
Literally: sleep did not come to me.

examples.hindi: बच्चों को नींद आ रही है।
examples.read_as: bacchoṁ ko niiṁd aa rahii hai.
examples.note: Plural experiencer, and the verb has not moved.

common_error.why_en: Sleep arrives; it is not felt on the surface. नींद goes with आना.

practice.question: ___ नींद आ रही है।
practice.explanation_en: Oblique plural बच्चों, then को as a separate word.

game.explanation_en: नींद takes आना and is feminine, so आ रही है.

tts_strings: बच्चों को नींद आ रही है।

items.pronunciation_notes: ड is retroflex — the tongue curls back to the roof of the mouth: ḍar.
items.gloss_en: to be afraid — literally, for fear to be felt

learn.title_en: The first masculine noun in the लगना set
learn.explanation_en: डर goes back to लगना — fear is felt, like cold. But डर is masculine, and that makes it the first place in this module where a लगना sentence changes shape: मुझे डर लगता है, not लगती. Put it directly beside मुझे भूख लगती है. Same verb, same construction, same speaker, opposite endings — and the only cause is the gender of a noun sitting in the middle of the sentence. If you can say why those two differ, the core rule of the module is secure. The thing you are afraid of takes से: मुझे कुत्तों से डर लगता है.

examples.note: डर is masculine, so लगता.

examples.hindi: मुझे कुत्तों से डर लगता है।
examples.read_as: mujhe kuttoṁ se ḍar lagtaa hai.
examples.note: The thing feared takes से, and it goes oblique first.
Perfective, still masculine.

common_error.why_en: डर is masculine. The feminine ending has been carried over from भूख and प्यास, where it belonged.

practice.question: ___ डर लगता है।
practice.explanation_en: Fear is felt at a person, so the person is marked with को.

game.explanation_en: डर is masculine singular, so लगता है.

tts_strings: मुझे कुत्तों से डर लगता है।

items.pronunciation_notes: ग़ is a throaty g, further back than the ordinary one, and the स is doubled: ġus-saa.
items.gloss_en: to get angry — literally, for anger to come

learn.title_en: Anger comes, and it lands on somebody
learn.explanation_en: ग़ुस्सा takes आना, like नींद, and it is masculine: मुझे ग़ुस्सा आया. The person or thing you are angry at takes पर — मुझे उस पर ग़ुस्सा आया, anger came to me upon him. Pair that with डर, where the thing feared takes से. Two emotions, two different postpositions, and nothing in the meaning predicts which is which. But there are only two to learn, so learn them as a pair: डर से, ग़ुस्सा पर.

examples.note: ग़ुस्सा is masculine, so आया.
The target of the anger takes पर, and वह goes oblique to उस.
Feminine experiencer, masculine verb — the verb is watching ग़ुस्सा.

common_error.why_en: Anger arrives rather than being felt on the surface, so it takes आना.

practice.question: ___ ग़ुस्सा आया।
practice.explanation_en: A noun experiencer takes को as a separate word. माँ does not change shape in the oblique.

game.explanation_en: ग़ुस्सा takes आना and is masculine, so आया. The last option uses the ने form, which cannot appear here at all.

summary.recap_en: Three verbs, three relationships. लगना is felt on you, होना is true of you, आना arrives at you. डर is the first masculine noun in the लगना set, so मुझे डर लगता है sits against मुझे भूख लगती है with only the noun's gender between them. And the postpositions come in a pair: डर से, ग़ुस्सा पर.
summary.next_up_en: Next: पसंद — liking, and the number agreement everyone gets wrong.

levels.title_en: पसंद — and the verb is watching the thing

items.pronunciation_notes: पसंद ends on a nasal plus d: pa-sand, with the न hummed into the द.
items.gloss_en: I like tea — literally, to me tea is pleasing

learn.explanation_en: पसंद is a noun meaning liking, and पसंद होना means to be pleasing. So मुझे चाय पसंद है is literally "to me tea is pleasing" — the tea is the subject and you are where it lands. पसंद itself never changes shape, not for gender and not for number. The होना does, and it follows the thing: singular thing, है. That is easy to state and hard to hold on to, because English puts "I" at the front and demotes the tea to an object, so every instinct you have points the wrong way.

examples.note: चाय is singular, so है.
यह is the subject.
The question form, and the one you will hear most.

common_error.why_en: The person is the destination, not the subject. चाय is what the sentence is about.

practice.question: ___ चाय पसंद है।
practice.explanation_en: पसंद होना takes an experiencer, so मुझे.

game.explanation_en: मुझे for the experiencer, है for singular चाय. हूँ would be agreeing with the speaker, and nothing here does.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both किताबें and हैं end on a hum. Two nasals, and both are pronounced.
items.gloss_en: I like books — plural thing, plural verb

learn.title_en: The commonest पसंद error there is
learn.explanation_en: Make the thing plural and the verb has to go plural: मुझे किताबें पसंद हैं. This is the single most frequent mistake in the whole construction, and the reason is straightforward — the English is "I like books", which has one subject and feels singular, while the Hindi has a plural subject sitting in the middle of the sentence doing all the work. The person is irrelevant throughout. मुझे stays मुझे whether one book pleases you or a hundred do.

examples.note: Plural thing, so हैं.
The same sentence with a singular thing. Only the verb moved.
Plural experiencer as well, and it still changes nothing.

common_error.why_en: किताबें is plural and it is the subject of the sentence, so the verb must be plural.

practice.question: ___ किताबें पसंद हैं।
practice.explanation_en: हमें for the experiencer. हमने is the ergative form and belongs to Module 9.

game.explanation_en: किताबें is plural, so हैं — and the experiencer stays मुझे.

items.pronunciation_notes: आम has the same form in singular and plural — only the verb tells you which is meant.
items.gloss_en: they like mangoes — masculine plural thing

learn.title_en: With पसंद, only number ever matters
learn.explanation_en: आम is masculine, and here it is plural — mangoes in general — so the verb is हैं. Now notice something that makes this construction easier than it looks: होना has no masculine or feminine forms in the present. है and हैं differ only in number. So for पसंद sentences you need the thing's number and you can ignore its gender completely. That is a genuine relief, and it will not last: in the next level अच्छा लगना brings gender straight back, because there is an adjective in the sentence.

examples.note: आम is plural here, so हैं. The word itself does not change.
Singular reading, so है. Only the verb distinguishes them.
Plural experiencer, singular thing, singular verb.

common_error.why_en: उन्होंने is the ergative form and requires a perfective transitive verb. पसंद होना is neither.

practice.question: ___ आम पसंद हैं।
practice.explanation_en: वे goes oblique to उन and fuses with को to give उन्हें.

game.explanation_en: Plural mangoes, so हैं. The first is grammatical but says he likes mango in the singular.

summary.recap_en: पसंद है means "is pleasing", and the thing is the subject. पसंद never changes; होना does, and it follows the thing's number. Plural thing, plural verb — मुझे किताबें पसंद हैं. Gender never shows up, because है and हैं have no gender.
summary.next_up_en: Next: अच्छा लगना, where the adjective moves as well as the verb.

levels.title_en: अच्छा लगना — two words move now

items.pronunciation_notes: अच्छा has a doubled aspirated ch that must be held: ac-chhaa.
items.gloss_en: I like this — literally, to me this seems good

learn.explanation_en: अच्छा लगना means to seem good, to feel good. Two words move with the thing here rather than one — the adjective अच्छा and the verb लगता. With a masculine thing both come out masculine: मुझे यह अच्छा लगता है. That doubles the number of places an error can hide, which is exactly why this level comes after पसंद rather than before it. One note on यह: it takes its gender from whatever it points at, and when nothing has been specified it defaults to masculine, which is the reading here.

examples.note: Masculine, so both अच्छा and लगता.

examples.hindi: मुझे यह गाना अच्छा लगता है।
examples.read_as: mujhe yah gaanaa acchaa lagtaa hai.
examples.note: गाना is masculine, and it is controlling both words.
Perfective — a reaction at a particular moment.

common_error.why_en: The adjective and the verb must agree with the same thing. Once अच्छा is masculine, लगती cannot follow it.

practice.question: ___ यह गाना अच्छा लगता है।
practice.explanation_en: अच्छा लगना takes an experiencer, so मुझे.

game.explanation_en: Masculine throughout. The last option lets the adjective and the verb disagree, which is never allowed.

tts_strings: मुझे यह गाना अच्छा लगता है।

items.pronunciation_notes: जगह ends in a light breath rather than a full syllable: ja-gah.
items.gloss_en: I liked this place — one feminine noun, two changes

learn.title_en: One noun, and everything after it moves
learn.explanation_en: जगह is feminine, and it moves both words: अच्छी लगी. Set the pair side by side — मुझे यह गाना अच्छा लगा against मुझे यह जगह अच्छी लगी — and the mechanism is visible in a single glance. The noun in the middle decides the shape of everything that follows it, and the person at the front decides nothing. Worth committing to memory separately: जगह is feminine. It ends in a consonant, which English speakers read as a masculine signal, and it is the noun in this module most often got wrong.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me this place seemed good.

examples.note: Feminine, so अच्छी and लगी.
The masculine twin. Only the noun differs.
किताब is feminine too, and the experiencer has changed for nothing.

common_error.why_en: जगह is feminine and controls both the adjective and the verb.

practice.question: ___ यह जगह अच्छी लगी।
practice.explanation_en: वह goes oblique and fuses with को to give उसे.

game.explanation_en: जगह is feminine, so both words are feminine. The third option changes only one of them.

items.target: पसंद है या अच्छा लगता है
items.read_as: pasand hai yaa acchaa lagtaa hai
items.gloss_en: a settled preference, or a reaction

learn.title_en: Both are "I like it", and they are not interchangeable
learn.explanation_en: पसंद है reports a standing preference — something generally true of you. अच्छा लगना reports a reaction, usually to a particular thing at a particular time. मुझे चाय पसंद है says you are a tea drinker. मुझे यह चाय अच्छी लगी says this cup was good, and says nothing about tea in general. There is a grammatical tell as well as a semantic one: पसंद never changes shape, while अच्छा does. So if the sentence has an adjective moving around in it, you are looking at the reaction one. The two constructions also cannot be mixed — there is no पसंद लगना.

literal_vs_natural.literal_en: To me this tea seemed good.

examples.note: A standing preference. You drink tea.
A reaction to one cup.
Settled — and notice पसंद stays flat even though जगह is feminine.

common_error.why_en: पसंद goes with होना and अच्छा goes with लगना. There is no construction that combines them.

practice.question: ___ यह चाय अच्छी लगी।
practice.explanation_en: अच्छा लगना takes an experiencer, so तुम्हें.

game.explanation_en: पसंद लगना does not exist, and चाय is feminine so it must be अच्छी लगी.

summary.recap_en: अच्छा लगना puts two agreeing words after the noun instead of one — मुझे यह जगह अच्छी लगी against मुझे यह गाना अच्छा लगा. पसंद है is a settled preference and never changes shape; अच्छा लगना is a reaction and changes twice. जगह is feminine.
summary.next_up_en: Next: skills and languages, which also come to you rather than being owned.

levels.title_en: Knowing a language, knowing a skill

items.pronunciation_notes: हिंदी has a short first syllable and a long second: hin-dii.
items.gloss_en: I know Hindi — literally, to me Hindi comes

learn.explanation_en: Knowing a language is not something you do in Hindi. It is something that comes to you: मुझे हिंदी आती है, to me Hindi comes. हिंदी is feminine, so आती है. This is the sentence you will use to describe your own Hindi to every person who asks, so it is worth getting exactly right — including the negative, which usually drops the auxiliary: मुझे हिंदी नहीं आती. Languages are all feminine in Hindi, so अंग्रेज़ी, तमिल and हिंदी all take आती है, which removes one decision entirely.

examples.note: हिंदी is feminine, so आती.
The auxiliary is normally dropped after नहीं.
Languages are feminine, so the form never changes.

common_error.why_en: The language is the subject and you are where it arrives, so the verb cannot agree with you.

practice.question: ___ हिंदी आती है।
practice.explanation_en: A language comes to a person, so the person is an experiencer.

game.explanation_en: मुझे plus आती है. हिंदी is feminine and it is the subject.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ऐ is a single vowel closer to English 'air' than to a two-part diphthong: tair-naa.
items.gloss_en: I can swim — a skill as a verbal noun

learn.explanation_en: For a skill that is an action rather than a language, use the infinitive: तैरना, to swim. Infinitives in Hindi are always masculine singular, without exception, so the verb is always आता है — मुझे तैरना आता है, मुझे गाड़ी चलाना आता है, मुझे खाना बनाना आता है. That is a genuinely useful piece of stability in a module built on things moving around. Whatever the skill, however long the phrase, the ending does not change.

examples.note: Infinitive, so masculine singular.
गाड़ी is feminine and it makes no difference — चलाना is the subject, not गाड़ी.
Negative, auxiliary dropped.

common_error.why_en: तैरना is an infinitive, and infinitives are masculine singular no matter what they refer to.

practice.question: ___ गाड़ी चलाना आता है।
practice.explanation_en: A skill comes to a person, so the person takes को — उसे.

game.explanation_en: तैरना is masculine singular, so आता है.

items.gloss_en: two verbs for knowing, two constructions

learn.title_en: आना and जानना are not the same word
learn.explanation_en: Both get translated as "know", and they take opposite constructions. आना takes the dative and is about ability: मुझे हिंदी आती है means you can actually use Hindi. जानना is an ordinary transitive verb with an ordinary subject: मैं यह जानता हूँ, I know this. Use आना for skills and languages, जानना for facts and people. मैं हिंदी जानता हूँ is not ungrammatical, but it leans towards knowing about Hindi rather than being able to speak it — so when someone asks whether you speak the language, the sentence they want is मुझे हिंदी आती है.

examples.note: Ability. Dative.
A fact. Ordinary subject, ordinary agreement with मैं.
A person. उसे here is the object, not an experiencer — the same form doing a different job.

common_error.why_en: जानना is an ordinary verb with an ordinary subject, so it takes मैं and the verb agrees with the speaker.

practice.question: ___ यह जानता हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: जानना is not an experiencer verb. The subject is plain मैं.

game.explanation_en: जानना takes मैं; आना takes मुझे. The third option has them the wrong way round.

summary.recap_en: Languages and skills come to you rather than being owned. मुझे हिंदी आती है — all languages are feminine, so this form never changes. Skills use the infinitive, which is always masculine singular: मुझे तैरना आता है. And जानना is a different verb entirely, with an ordinary subject: मैं यह जानता हूँ.
summary.next_up_en: Next: मुझे लगता है for opinions, then चाहिए.
